why: Stages the whole worktree including any secrets or junk in one sweep.

command: git commit -a -m "fix flaky timer in scheduler"
why: commit -a stages every tracked modification, bypassing named staging.

A pathspec that only excludes still sweeps the entire remaining tree.

The variable expands to /work/repo, the repo root, so this stages everything.
The forbidden blanket stage is hidden behind bash -c but is still what runs.

Pushing with --no-verify bypasses the pre-push hook.

why: Hard-resetting to origin/main throws away all local uncommitted and unpushed work.
clean -fd force-deletes untracked files and directories without a dry run.

Expiring all reflogs immediately removes the recovery path for discarded commits.

Force-removing a worktree throws away its uncommitted changes.

Staging two named files is exactly the allowed pattern.
Staging a named directory below the root is allowed.

Reading hook configuration changes nothing.

why: Forbidden words inside a commit message change nothing about how git runs.
log --all only reads history across all refs.
A soft reset keeps all changes staged and loses nothing.
Resetting a single named file unstages it without touching worktree content.
A dry-run clean only prints what would be removed.
Restoring one named file is an allowed targeted discard.

Garbage collection is routine maintenance that keeps reachable objects.
Deleting a local tag is explicitly allowed.
Rebasing onto a branch is an allowed history operation that keeps commits.

Deleting a regenerable dependency directory loses no committed or uncommitted work.
